results.name: Exercise Ball Back Stretch
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, and your hands resting on your thighs.
Slowly walk your feet forward and roll your body down the ball, allowing your back to drape over the ball until your lower back is supported.
Extend your arms at your sides, allowing them to hang naturally to the floor, and relax into the stretch, letting your spine gently curve over the ball.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and allowing your back muscles to relax.
tips: Ensure your feet are firmly planted on the floor to maintain stability and balance.
Use a properly inflated exercise ball to ensure it supports your weight and provides a comfortable stretch.
Focus on relaxing your back and letting your spine naturally curve over the ball.
Breathe deeply and steadily, inhaling through your nose and exhaling through your mouth to enhance relaxation.
results.description: Exercise Ball Back Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders.

results.name: Exercise Ball Hip Flexor Stretch
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball in a lunge position with your left foot flat on the floor in front of you and your right leg extended behind you, the ball supporting your hips.
Lower your hips downwards towards the floor, allowing the ball to support your weight and feeling a stretch in your right hip flexor.
Keep your torso upright and your core engaged as you hold the stretch.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then switch legs and repeat on the other side.
tips: Move slowly into the stretch to prevent overextending or causing discomfort.
Breathe deeply and steadily, focusing on relaxing the hip flexor muscles.
Use a properly inflated exercise ball to provide adequate support for your hips.
results.description: Exercise Ball Hip Flexor Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Quadriceps.

results.name: Exercise Ball Lat Stretch
instructions: Begin on the floor in a tabletop position with your hands and knees on the floor.
Have an exercise ball on your right side and position your right hand on the ball, keeping your arm bent at 90 degrees.
Slowly roll the ball forward with your right hand, extending your right arm overhead and lowering your chest lightly towards the floor, feeling the stretch along your back.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, then slowly roll the ball back towards you to return to the starting position. Repeat on the left side.
tips: Ensure your hips remain above your knees to maintain proper form and support.
Move slowly into the stretch to prevent overextending or causing discomfort.
Use a properly inflated exercise ball to provide adequate support for your arm.
results.description: Exercise Ball Lat Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Shoulders, Upper Back.

results.name: Exercise Ball Lower Back Dynamic Stretch
instructions: Begin on your hands and feet with your arms and legs straight, positioning an exercise ball under your hips.
Slowly lower your body onto the ball, allowing it to support your hips and torso, while keeping your arms and legs straight and your hips bent.
Relax into the stretch for a second, letting your back gently arch over the ball and feeling a stretch in your lower back.
Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you lower onto the ball and exhaling as you return to the starting position.
Ensure the exercise ball is properly inflated to provide adequate support and facilitate smooth movement.
Avoid overextending your back; only lower onto the ball as far as is comfortable without causing strain.
results.description: Exercise Ball Lower Back Dynamic Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders.

instructions: Begin on your hands and feet with your arms and legs straight, positioning an exercise ball under your hips.
Slowly lower your body onto the ball, allowing it to support your hips and torso, while keeping your arms and legs straight and your hips bent.
Relax into the stretch, letting your back gently arch over the ball and feeling a stretch in your lower back.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you lower onto the ball and exhaling as you return to the starting position.
Ensure the exercise ball is properly inflated to provide adequate support and facilitate smooth movement.
Avoid overextending your back; only lower onto the ball as far as is comfortable without causing strain.
results.description: Exercise Ball Lower Back Prone Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the spine (back). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Shoulders.

results.name: Exercise Ball Lying Side Lat Stretch (Variation 2)
instructions: Begin by lying on your side with an exercise ball positioned under your armpit and lower ribs. Extend your top leg straight and bend your lower leg, placing the foot flat on the floor for stability.
Allow your bottom arm to hang in a comfortable position for support over the ball and extend your left arm overhead, reaching it along the line of your body.
Allow your body to relax over the ball, feeling a stretch along the side of your torso and through your latissimus dorsi (lats).
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily. Slowly roll back to the starting position and repeat on the other side.
tips: Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you extend into the stretch and exhaling as you hold the stretch.
Avoid overextending your back; only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing strain.
Make sure your top leg is firmly planted on the floor to provide stability and support.
results.description: Exercise Ball Lying Side Lat Stretch (Variation 2) is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the lats (back). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Obliques, Shoulders.

instructions: Begin by lying on your side with an exercise ball positioned under your armpit and lower ribs. Extend your top leg straight and bend your lower leg, placing the foot flat on the floor for stability.

results.name: Exercise Ball Seated Hamstring Stretch
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart, and your back straight.
Extend your right leg straight out in front of you, keeping your heel on the floor and your toes pointing up.
Slowly hinge at your hips, leaning forward while keeping your back straight, and reach towards your right toes with your right hand. Feel the stretch along the back of your right leg (hamstring).
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily. Return to the starting position and repeat with your left leg.
tips: Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you prepare to stretch and exhaling as you lean forward.
Only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing pain or discomfort.
Ensure the exercise ball is properly inflated to provide adequate support and stability.
results.description: Exercise Ball Seated Hamstring Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the hamstrings (upper legs). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Calves.

results.name: Exercise Ball Seated Quad Stretch
instructions: Sit on an exercise ball with your feet flat on the floor, hip-width apart.
Slowly roll forward until your back is supported on the ball, keeping your shoulders and head relaxed on the ball, and place your arms at your sides for balance.
Bend your left leg with your foot flat on the floor for support. Bend your right leg, placing the forefoot on the floor and the heel on the ball to feel the stretch in your right quadriceps.
Hold the stretch for 15-30 seconds, breathing deeply and steadily. Slowly return to the starting position and repeat with the opposite leg.
tips: Focus on deep, steady breathing, inhaling as you prepare to stretch and exhaling as you hold the stretch.
Only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing pain or discomfort.
Ensure the exercise ball is properly inflated to provide adequate support and stability.
results.description: Exercise Ball Seated Quad Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the quads (upper legs). Performed with a stability ball, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Hip Flexors.

results.name: Extension and Inclination Neck Stretch
instructions: Stand with your back straight and shoulders relaxed.
Slowly rotate your head to the left side while diagonally lowering your head, bringing your chin towards your left shoulder to feel a stretch in your neck.
Hold the stretch for a few seconds, breathing deeply and steadily.

Return to the neutral position and repeat on the other side by rotating your head to the right and diagonally lowering your head towards your right shoulder. Repeat for the desired number of repetitions.
tips: Maintain good posture with your back straight and shoulders relaxed throughout the exercise.
Perform the stretches in a smooth, fluid motion to enhance flexibility and reduce muscle tension.
Avoid overextending your neck; only stretch as far as is comfortable without causing pain or discomfort.
results.description: Extension and Inclination Neck Stretch is a beginner single-joint isolation static exercise targeting the levator scapulae (neck). Performed with bodyweight, it falls under the flexibility category. Secondary muscles: Upper Back, Neck.
